title: March 2019 bomb cyclone flooding - Eastern Nebraska (Lincoln / Omaha / Elkhorn), March 13-18, 2019
disclaimer: HISTORICAL REPLAY. Every alert, text and observation here is an archived real National Weather Service / IEM record from March 2019, selected by time filter and replayed. It is NOT live data and must never be presented as a current alert. Road closures are not included (no archived 511 data was available).

facts.event: Mid-March 2019 'bomb cyclone' and eastern Nebraska flooding (rain and rapid snowmelt on frozen ground)
facts.bomb_cyclone: Deepened 24 mb in 15 h, from 994 mb to about 970 mb, on March 12-13, 2019 (NWS Hastings/GID).
facts.weather_window: From March 12-14 a rapidly deepening low brought heavy rain, warm temperatures and dense fog with rapid snow/ice melt; ground was frozen deeper than 2 feet (NWS flood-safety page for Nebraska).
facts.blizzard_note: Blizzard conditions on the morning of March 14 occurred in central Nebraska (e.g. Ord), per NWS Hastings; the OAX archive has NO blizzard or winter storm product covering the Lincoln/Omaha facility locations.
impacts: Nearly 50 levees were breached on the Platte, Elkhorn and Missouri Rivers (NWS).
A Platte River levee breach near Leshara forced the evacuation of NWS Omaha/Valley (NWS).
Valley and Fremont, NE were cut off from the rest of the state for a time by flooded roads (NWS Central Region).
About one-third of Offutt Air Force Base was flooded; Interstate 29 south of Omaha remained closed (NWS Central Region).
facts.weekdays: Wed Mar 13, Thu Mar 14, Fri Mar 15 and Mon Mar 18, 2019 were all normal work days.

The National Weather Service in Omaha has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
  West central Platte County in northeastern Nebraska...
  Southern Boone County in northeastern Nebraska...

* Until 1215 AM CDT.

* At 616 PM CDT, local law enforcement reported ongoing extensive 
  flooding of the Cedar River and Beaver Creek. Many roads have been 
  closed throughout the area, and travel is not advised. Additional 
  rainfall moving through the area, will only exacerbate current 
  problems. 

* Some locations that will experience flooding include...
  St. Edward, Cedar Rapids and The Highway 14 And 56 Junction. 

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

A Flash Flood Warning means that flooding is imminent or occurring.
If you are in the warned area move to higher ground immediately.
Residents living along streams and creeks should take immediate
precautions to protect life and property.
